answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated trades whose counterparties have independently bonded scarce collateral and stayed solvent through settlement. A sybil can mint many names, but each must lock capital, and fake trades between its own identities do not count because counterparties must be unrelated and risk loss on default. The plume of new accounts, even tagged yarrow or umber, therefore buys no trust; the attacker pays in tied-up funds and exposure to real losses.
